title: Research consolidation: bind CITATION/CONTRIBUTING/CONTRIBUTORS to the selected record (no new kappa)
body:
**Research consolidation + tooling. No new κ.** This PR does not change the certificate, construction, selected record or frontier.

Base: `9a16422bf8d0ebd3342c1156c33cb5703c6cb02a`. Sprint track 95–99 (consolidation), seed 98.

## Discrepancy

`certificates/selected-result.json` selects PR890 with PR589 at κ = 0.001661957774647029, with replay command `make frontier890-verify`. README.md and current-status.md agree with it. At base, three other public entry points did not:

- **`CITATION.cff`**, which GitHub's "Cite this repository" reads, still said "selected checkpoint is PR626 with PR543" and gave κ = 51110230636731/31250000000000000. That is two selections stale, and it credits the wrong bit supplier.
- **`CONTRIBUTING.md`** still pointed to `community-frontier741-review.md` and "currently `make frontier741-verify`".
- **`CONTRIBUTORS.md`** headline still said "Current reviewed composition: #799 with #589".

## This keeps happening

`research/selected-entrypoint-drift/history.py` runs the same unchanged binder against all 17 commits that changed the selected record, plus the base. **12 of the 17 selection commits left at least one restatement that contradicted the record committed with it:**

| File | Number of selection commits where it contradicted the record |
|---|---|
| CONTRIBUTING.md | 9 |
| CITATION.cff | 7 |
| CONTRIBUTORS.md | 1 |
| current-status.md | 1 |
| README.md | 0 |

I checked every contradiction against the text at that commit. Cases where the old wording had no anchor phrase (`missing`) are not counted as agreement or as drift. One false positive, README's older `\times10^{-4}` notation, was found during review. The parser now handles it and a test covers it.

## Change

- `CITATION.cff`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the `CONTRIBUTORS.md` headline now match the selected record, README and the #890 review. The existing cumulative contributor table is now labelled "SW4 and X4 rounds through #799". No credit text was removed.
- `scripts/verify_selected_entrypoints.py` checks 18 fields across these files against the record: exact κ and decimal, the primary PR, review and receipt links, and the replay command. It also checks that `reproduce` is a real Makefile target and that `previous_kappa` matches its checkpoint. A missing anchor fails, and decimals are compared exactly. It complements `scripts/verify_selected_result.py`.
- `tests/test_selected_entrypoints.py` adds 7 tests with negative controls. Each stale base value is rejected on exactly the expected fields. Rounded decimals, missing anchors, an undefined target, a wrong previous κ and an underivable primary PR are also rejected. `make verify-tests` picks the tests up automatically. No Makefile or workflow edits.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -I -B scripts/verify_selected_entrypoints.py
# PASS 18 selected-result restatements agree with certificates/selected-result.json: kappa 1661957774647029/1000000000000000000
```

On a checkout of the base commit, the same command (`--root <base checkout>`) exits 1 with `FAIL 8 of 18`. Further commands:

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_selected_entrypoints.py -v   # 7 tests OK
python3 -I -B research/selected-entrypoint-drift/history.py --check        # needs a non-shallow clone
```

Checks run locally (Fedora, Python 3.14; the new checks also passed on 3.12):
- `make selected-record-check` passes, and so do the existing `test_selected_result.py` tests.
- `make verify-tests`: 93 of 94 modules pass, including the new one. The exception is `test_cpp_headers.py`, which needs a `c++` compiler that this machine lacks. It fails identically on the untouched base. I did not run frontier replays, because no construction input changed.

## Scope and open questions

- This is a metadata consistency check only. It does not replay or certify κ, and it does not decide what should be selected; the record is authoritative. Prose credit lists are not mechanically checked.
- The CITATION `version`/`date-released` follow the existing `community-<audit>-<date>` pattern. The maintainer should confirm them, because they cannot be derived from the record.
- The binder is **not** wired into `selected-record-check`, so frontier replays don't depend on documentation text. The maintainer may choose to wire it in.
- Noted and left unchanged: `make verify` still invokes `frontier741-verify`, not the selected `frontier890-verify`. That may be intentional for cost. Ledger coverage of the selected source PRs is navinor's open #867 and is not duplicated here.

## Credit

This builds on the maintainer's `verify_selected_result.py` and selection records. It is related to #841 (Mihir Srivastava, digest-bound proof pointers) and #867 (navinor, ledger coverage map).
